newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends lower ahead of API data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends lower ahead of API data.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices extended their declines Tuesday on expectations that weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) will show significant increases in crude and gasoline supply.
"There was some position-squaring ahead of the API stats tonight. We expect crude stocks will grow after falling so much last week," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives in New York.
February gasoline suffered the worst losses, settling off 1.05 cents a gallon at 67.04 cents.
Feb crude ended off eight cents a barrel at $25.11 while Feb heating oil ended off 0.28 cent a gallon at 69.42 cents.

Due to weak demand and refineries stockpiling product to avoid getting caught short during seasonal maintenance in January, traders expected gasoline stocks to have risen more than two million barrels for the week ended January 10.

Crude stocks were also seen rising more than two million barrels due to an increase in imports. Crude stocks dropped by 9.5 million barrels a week earlier due in part to year-end tax maneuvering as refiners in the U.S. Gulf are taxed on the amount of crude they hold, dealers said.

Heating oil prices, however, were supported by forecasts Tuesday calling for an extended period of much below normal temperatures in the "heating oil belt" of the northeastern United States starting this weekend.

After milder temperatures this week, the National Weather Service sees temperatures in both the Northeast and in Texas to be least six degrees below the seasonal average in its six-to-10 day forecast starting on January 19.
The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
